units.name: Gendarmerie
units.desc: The Gendarmerie are the elite cavalry of the realm, recruited from the most prestigious noble families. Clad in cuirasses and armed with the finest swords and pistols, they are a formidable force on the battlefield.

units.name: Provincial Cavalry
units.desc: Formed of countryside gentry fulfilling their obligations, the Provincial Cavalry are a competent force of mounted aristocrats.

units.name: Late Cavaliers
units.desc: The Late Cavaliers are the last vestiges of mounted nobility on the battlefield, clad in half-armor and wielding pistols and sabers.

units.name: Cavaliers
units.desc: The golden age of knighthood may be over, but the Nobility retains a presence on the battlefield as a gallant and well-armed cavalry force.

units.name: Plated Knights
units.desc: Encased in the finest suits of steel armor, these noblemen fight from horseback with maces and hammers designed to crack open helmets and breastplates.

units.name: Teulu
units.desc: A marriage of the Celtic and Continental martial traditions, the Teulu are mounted knights who nimbly dominate rough terrain.
units.whoText: Culture: Cornish, Welsh

units.name: Mailed Knights
units.desc: Adorned with brightly-colored regalia and fluttering pennants, Mailed Knights are a sight to behold in any army. But it is their shimmering mail and sharpened steel, along with a lifetime of training, that makes them amongst the hardiest warriors on the battlefield.

units.name: Noble Cavalry
units.desc: Riding a horse into battle has long been a status symbol amongst the powerful.

units.name: Crusader Knights
units.desc: In a knightly order, its members are required to be proficient in combat, and serve the order's interest in battle. Thus, the Crusader Knights are the best mounted soldiers any order can offer.
units.whoText: Can raise crusader levies

units.name: Crusader Knights
units.desc: In a knightly order, its members are required to be proficient in combat, and serve the order's interest in battle. Thus, the Crusader Knights are the best mounted soldiers any order can offer.
units.whoText: Can recruit crusader regiments

units.name: Order Knights
units.desc: The Order Knights are the most experienced and skilled mounted knights of the order, often leading relatevely small, but skilled units of very heavily armored horsemen into battle under the banner of their Military Order.
units.whoText: Can raise crusader levies

units.name: Order Knights
units.desc: The Order Knights are the most experienced and skilled mounted knights of the order, often leading relatevely small, but skilled units of very heavily armored horsemen into battle under the banner of their Military Order.
units.whoText: Has institution = Professional Armies; Can recruit crusader regiments

units.name: Moa Hunters
units.desc: A lifetime of stalking giant moa birds in the rough interior has forged these huntsmen into particularly adept skirmishers.
units.whoText: (Has owner = No or government: Tribe); (region: New Zealand and Raw material = Wild Game and (country type: Pop or government: Tribe))

units.name: Tribesmen
units.desc: Brandishing a variety of implements and simple weapons, Tribesmen are agrarian villagers raised to protect their homes and their kin.

units.name: Warriors
units.desc: Warriors are the name given to tribal fighters following the command of their leaders. Their weaponry can vary depending on their origins, but can be considered somewhat simple, yet effective.
units.whoText: (Has owner = No or government: Tribe)

units.name: Champions
units.desc: Champions are elite units among tribal warriors, formed by those that stand out among the ranks of the Warriors for their bravery and martial abilities
units.whoText: (country type: Pop or government: Tribe)

units.name: Chieftains
units.desc: Noble warriors adorned in decorative armor and wielding bejeweled weaponry, Chieftains are expected to lead the charge and serve as exemplars to the other fighters.
units.whoText: (Has owner = No or government: Tribe); (country type: Pop or government: Tribe)

units.name: Villagers
units.desc: This unit, formed by armed peasants without military training, is no more than a desperate attempt to face enemies, a last line of defense against an invader force.

units.name: Feudal Levies
units.desc: A Feudal Levies is formed by peasants that are drafted in times of war as part of their duty towards their feudal lord, and have some military training. These levies are to eventually be replaced by professional armies.

units.name: Crusader Sergeants
units.desc: Warrior monks devoted to the expansion of Christendom, the Crusader Sergeants form the elite foot vanguard of the religious military orders, pairing the Crusader Knights on foot.
units.whoText: Can raise crusader levies

units.name: Crusader Sergeants
units.desc: Warrior monks devoted to the expansion of Christendom, the Crusader Sergeants form the elite foot vanguard of the religious military orders, pairing the Crusader Knights on foot.
units.whoText: Can recruit crusader regiments

units.name: Caterans
units.desc: Caterans are very light raiders armed with short spears and handaxes. Other than small targes and skullcaps, they are unencumbered by armor, relying instead on their swiftness for defense.
units.whoText: (culture group: Scottish and culture group: Celtic)

units.name: Kerns
units.desc: Bands of skirmishers borne of the rugged hills and peaty bogs, Kerns are light raiders armed with darts and daggers.
units.whoText: (culture group: Hibernian and culture group: Celtic)

units.name: Lour Lances
units.desc: The so-called \"galoys ove lour lances\" are light infantry famed for their agile use of heavy spears. Once the scrummage inevitably collapses, they brandish great knives to finish off more heavily-armored foes.
units.whoText: Culture: Welsh, Cornish; Culture: Cornish, Welsh

units.name: Schiltron
units.desc: A bristling wall of pikes and shields, a Schiltron can hold fast against charges at the cost of mobility.
units.whoText: Any pop …; Culture: Scots, Highland, Norse-Gael

units.name: Horse Archers
units.desc: Riders from the Steppes have specialized in two ways of mounted combat: lances or archery. For the latter, the development of stronger but smaller bows has given them the mobility of the horses and the accuracy and fast volley that short bows provide, making them ideal for hit-and-run tactics.

units.name: Steppe Horde Militia
units.desc: Mongol children are taught how to ride a horse and shoot a bow, and are expected to join the raiding bands when they grow up. In a Horde, men combine peasant activities during peacetime, usually consisting in pastoralism, and military duties whenever the leader of the tribe requires it.
units.whoText: Government: Steppe Horde

units.name: Tribal Cavalry
units.desc:
Many of the tribes living on the outskirts of our country base their existence around the raising and caring of horses and cattle, by living their whole lives around these animals, they are bound to raise great riders among their midst.

On the rare occasion when a strong hand manages to organize this unruly fighters into a semi coherent unit they form a fast and surprisingly effective force.

names: Has estate privilege = Allow Tribal Levies

units.whoText: (Has estate privilege = Allow Tribal Levies and not government: Steppe Horde and Market …)

units.name: A'Urughs
units.desc: A'Urughs are military administered familiar units and flocks left behind by the Mongolian armies.

units.name: Almogavars
units.desc: Almogavars are a class of light infantry soldiers originating from the Crown of Aragon. These quick-moving warriors serve as frontier defenders and foot soldiers. In addition to their role in the Reconquista, they have also found employment as mercenaries in Italy, the Frankokratia, and the Levant.
units.whoText: Culture: Aragonese, Catalan

units.name: Catalan Crossbowmen
units.desc: Some of the fiercest and deadliest crossbowmen in the Western Mediterranean, the Catalan Crossbowmen compete against the Genoese Crossbowmen for supremacy in this field.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; Culture: Catalan

units.name: Farfanes
units.desc: The Farfanes are Christian mercenaries employed by the states of Maghreb. They may be skilled, but their real asset is indifference to local power struggles: they stay loyal despite tribal bickering and fickle allegiances.
units.whoText: Reform: Catalan Merchant Privileges; Is capital

units.name: Navarrese Crossbowmen
units.desc: Renowned across Christendom for their marksmanship on the broken Pyrenean ground, the Navarrese Crossbowmen served as far afield as France and Italy in the Compañías Navarras of the fourteenth century. They are municipal companies before they are royal ones, townsmen who hold tax and jurisdictional privileges in return for their service, and kings who wanted crossbows hired them by the company.
units.whoText: Culture: Basque; (dlc: Across The Pillars and culture: Basque)

units.name: Warbows
units.desc: The powerful martial longbow, originally deployed with great impact against armored English knights in the Welsh valleys, has been adopted into the military doctrine on either side of the border.

units.desc: Mounted upon the agile Irish hobby horse, Hobelars are spearmen able to swiftly traverse rough terrain.

units.name: Gallowglass
units.desc: Heavy infantry fitted with mail and wielding two-handed axes, the fearsome Gallowglass descend from Norse sea raiders who settled along the Atlantic coast.

units.name: Light Jurchen Cavalry
units.desc: A light complement to our heavy cavalry, their role is to pursue routed enemies and cut them down.
units.whoText: Culture group: Jurchen

units.name: Iron Pagoda Cavalry
units.desc: Powerful and heavy cavalry set to punch through the enemy's frontline and deliver a deadly blow to their morale and formation.
units.whoText: Culture group: Jurchen

units.name: Early Paik
units.desc: Paiks are foot soldiers of India who are renowned for their offensive and defensive versatility and their skill in archery. Every man serves in the Paik System as a Paik conscript, which leads to a greater quantity of troops on the field, but comes at the cost of professionalism.
units.whoText: (culture group: Indian and Integration level = Integrated, Integration level = Core)

units.name: Early Paik Infantry
units.desc: Paiks are foot soldiers of India who are renowned for their offensive and defensive versatility and their skill in archery.
units.whoText: Global may build paik units; Culture group: Indian; Integration level = Integrated, Integration level = Core

units.name: Byzantine Cataphracts
units.desc: A powerful body of heavily armored knights, the Cataphracts make up the elite of our cavalry units. Armed with a short lance named 'kontos' and covered in scale armor, these troops strike fear at the heart of our enemies. A whirlwind of steel in the form of an unstoppable wave of horsemen delivers the killing blow to all those who seek to trample our people.
units.whoText: Culture group: Roman

units.name: Akritai
units.desc: The Akritai rose to prominence as the defenders of Anatolia against the eastern threats that the empire faced. These soldiers were given grants through the Decayed Theme System to cultivate and protect, as a means to provide them with a reward and a reason to defend our homeland.
units.whoText: Culture group: Roman

units.name: Varangian Guard
units.desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as pelekyphóroi bárbaroi, axe-wielding barbarians.
units.whoText: Country: Byzantium; Is capital

units.name: Early Mamālīk
units.desc: Well-trained elite troops, these men have been honed to represent the best our people have to offer. Raised as slaves purchased from foreign masters, they are disciplined and taught our religious and military doctrines as they are expected to form the core of our standing army. Oftentimes, they come equipped with heavy armor and sturdy spears. Their unique helmets and presence in the battlefield is a terrifying sight for our foes.

units.name: Mamālīk Horsemen
units.desc: The mounted arm of the Mamlūk military, these elite slave-soldier cavalry form the iconic shock force of our armies. Trained from youth in horsemanship, archery, and the lance, they complement the foot-based Early Mamālīk regiments and project the power of the sultanate across the battlefield.

units.name: Ḥalqah
units.desc: Auxiliary units that often accompanied their Mamlūk counterparts, these light and quick troops will offer great support to their parent forces on the battlefield.

units.name: Jonow Auxiliary
units.desc: The Jonow are slaves who accompany the Kèlè-Koun and their soldiers as carriers of their military equipment.

units.name: Sofa Infantrymen
units.desc: Slaves who were trained in the arts of war so they can serve the state as soldiers. Although they receive their weapons from the Horon (the free men of Mali), it is them who risk their lives in combat.
units.whoText: May build sofa units

units.name: Mandekalu Infantry
units.desc:
The Mandekalu Infantry are the backbone of the Malian military, and are made of the Horon - the free people of Mali. Equipped with javelins, bows and poisoned arrows, they are a formidable force to be reckoned with.

Can gain Experience in order to be promoted to Farari Infantry and Farari Cavalry after the advance Farari Corps has been researched. Experience is shared by all Mandekalu units. Won battles grant +15, lost battles grant +5 Experience per participating Mandekalu unit.

units.name: Mandekalu Horsemen
units.desc:
The Mandekalu Horsemen are the additional support of the Malian military. These Horon - the free people of Mali - received their mount and equipment from the Ton-tigi and the Mansa. Charging into the battle with lances and long swords, the Mandekalu Horsemen projected the power of the Mansa even in the furthest corners of the empire.

Can gain Experience in order to be promoted to Farari Infantry and Farari Cavalry after the advance Farari Corps has been researched. Experience is shared by all Mandekalu units. Won battles grant +15, lost battles grant +5 Experience per participating Mandekalu unit.

units.name: Farari Infantry
units.desc: The Farari are the elite corps of the Malian military. Appointed from privileged and common people alike, the Farari are known for their bravery and military experience.

units.name: Farari Cavalry
units.desc: The Farari are the elite corps of the Malian military. Appointed from privileged and common people alike, the Farari are known for their bravery and military experience.

units.name: Clan Retainers
units.desc: The key part of any clan's army are their close retainers, troops bounded by ties of loyalty and familiar relationships.
units.whoText: Culture group: Japanese; Country type: Building

units.name: Clan Retainer Cavalry
units.desc: The key part of any clan's army are their close retainers, troops bounded by ties of loyalty and familiar relationships.
units.whoText: Culture group: Japanese; Country type: Location

units.name: Hafsid Ghulām
units.desc: The Hafsid Ghulām are the slave-soldier corps of Hafsid Tunis: Black African captives from the trans-Saharan markets, Iberian prisoners from corsair raids, and children of earlier ghulām born to the institution and bound to the throne. They are the disciplined counterweight to the restless Banū Hilāl tribal levies.
units.whoText: Country: Tunis

units.name: Zayyanid Ghulām
units.desc: The Zayyanid Ghulām are the mamlūk-style slave retainers of the Zayyanid emirs of Tlemcen, bought from the Saharan caravan trade and Genoese factors at Oran, trained from boyhood, and sworn to the emir alone. They garrison the Mechouar fortress and form the emir's strike force when the tribes threaten the throne.
units.whoText: Country: Tlemcen

units.name: Iberian Jinetes
units.desc: The Iberian Jinetes are the light horse of Christian Iberia, adapted from the Andalusi jinete. Fast riders with javelin and light lance, they skirmish and harry across the broken country of the Meseta rather than charge home like heavy cavalry.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; Culture group: Iberian; not culture: Andalusi; Region: Iberia

units.name: Longbowmen
units.desc: The Longbowmen excel not only due to their powerful warbow but also their years of training on the archery fields.

units.desc: The gradual influence of continental-style warfare has led to better-equipped and more cohesive units of Gallowglass.

units.name: Wagenburg
units.desc: During the Hussite Wars, our armies relied on wagon forts called Wagenburg to win battles against superior forces. While we may not always deploy wagons, the principle remains: infantry sharpshooters fighting from prepared defensive positions become our standard doctrine.

units.name: Genoese Crossbowmen
units.desc: Genoese Crossbowmen are a respected military unit that was used by the Genoese during the First Crusade up until now. Equipped with Genoese crossbows and the pavise, these infantrymen serve as the protection of their home as well as mercenaries in Europe.
units.whoText: Culture: Ligurian

units.name: Reformed Almogavars
units.desc: The Almogavars, embracing new innovations, have undergone remarkable adaptations to enhance their efficiency on the battlefield. Integrating cutting-edge weaponry and strategic advancements into their traditional tactics, these formidable warriors have become even more formidable. With a blend of ancient expertise and modern tools, they stand as a prime example of the seamless fusion between tradition and innovation in warfare.
units.whoText: Culture: Aragonese, Catalan

units.name: Order Sergeants
units.desc: Adapting to the changing warfare, the Crusader Sergeants have adopted new tactics and refined weaponry. With these adaptions they will retain their status as the elite foot forces of the Military Orders, side by side with the Order Knights.
units.whoText: Has institution = Professional Armies; Can recruit crusader regiments

units.name: Order Sergeants
units.desc: Adapting to the changing warfare, the Crusader Sergeants have adopted new tactics and refined weaponry. With these adaptions they will retain their status as the elite foot forces of the Military Orders, side by side with the Order Knights.
units.whoText: Can raise crusader levies

units.name: Hwacha
units.desc: The Hwacha deliver devastating firepower through their barrages of rocket-powered arrows or iron-headed bolts. Their maneuverability forces them to take a more defensive role in battles.

units.name: Reformed Mamālīk
units.desc: The later Mamlūk troops are categorized by a renewed attention to detail and discipline. A series of military reforms are set in place, to restore the old standards and retrain our standing armies.

units.name: Reformed Mamālīk Horsemen
units.desc: Like their foot brethren, the mounted Mamālīk undergo renewed training and discipline reforms. The mounted core of our standing army remains the elite shock cavalry of the sultanate.

units.name: Serbian Hussars
units.desc: The Hussars are a light cavalry unit whose origin can be traced back to bands of mounted Serb warriors. Their light armor and fast horses allow them to outmaneuver any other regiment, opening the door to the development of innovative strategies.

units.name: Muslim Riders
units.desc: Unlike the infantry-based armies of Southern India, these Muslim Riders will allow for much more flexibility in battle.

ids: Has unlocked unit trigger: Type Muslim Riders
names: Has unlocked unit trigger: Type Muslim Riders

units.whoText: Has unlocked unit trigger: Type Muslim Riders; Religion: Sunnism, Shiism, Ibadism

units.name: Late Karambit Warriors
units.desc: Armed with rudimentary armor and their trademark blade, these warriors rely on mastering speed, ferocity, and fluent movements. They excel on close combat where the karambit's curved blade is extremely efficient at slashing, hooking, and gutting opponents. The adoption and proliferation of new formations and combat maneuvers has turned these warriors into a fabled armed force, feared throughout the archipelago.

units.name: Tuareg Veiled Cavalry
units.desc: The Tuareg Veiled Cavalry are the indigo-veiled camel-and-horse riders of the deep Sahara, grown out of the Tuareg Camelry into a heavier arm that can hold ground as well as raid. They carry the straight takouba broadsword and the long allagh lance, taking payment from the caravans they escort and plunder from those they do not.
units.whoText: Culture group: Amazigh, Maghrebi; Culture: Tuareg

units.name: Hungarian Black Army
units.desc: Serving as a standing mercenary army for the Kingdom of Hungary, Hungarian Black Army is a full-time war-focused army, in contrast to other mercenary armies across Europe. They use an unusually high ratio of fire weapons for the period.
units.whoText: Culture: Hungarian

units.name: Landsknechte
units.desc: The Landsknechte combine, in a same unit, pikemen with the infamous Doppelsöldner, 'double-pay men' carrying two-handed swords, while being supported by arquebusiers at their flanks.
units.whoText: Culture group: German

units.name: Late Gallowglass
units.desc: A blend of old and new, these Late Gallowglass are heavily-armored troops outfitted with a medley of modern weapons such as arquebus guns to complement their traditional greatswords and axes.

units.desc: Small innovations in equipment and organization result in continuous devastating volleys that shatter all but the most heavily armored formations.

units.name: Lanzas de Castilla
units.desc: Inspired by the Moorish jinete, the Lanzas de Castilla ride lighter than a knightly lance but fight heavier than a skirmisher, closing to break a formation where a true light horseman would only harass and withdraw.
units.whoText: Culture: Castilian

units.name: Akıncılar
units.desc: A unit of light cavalry that specializes in mobile and ranged warfare, these raiders make for a fine army and a valuable addition to our ranks.

units.name: Reisläufer
units.desc: Some of our countrymen elect to travel into foreign lands and earn their keep as mercenaries for foreign rulers. Once these return to their home, these men are veteran soldiers and some of the best fighters of Europe.
units.whoText: Culture group: Swiss

units.name: Cetbang
units.desc: One of the most prominent muzzle-loaded cannons of our era is the Cetbang. Armed with a cylindrical short barrel, it delivers a devastating blow with tremendous power. Such is its popularity, that it finds use in many aspects of our conduct of warfare, from protecting our ports to being the main armament of our warships and armies.

units.name: Dahomey Amazons
units.desc: A regiment of women that originate from Guinea. They strike fear into the enemy ranks, and cause devastating damage.

units.name: Esho Cavalry
units.desc: A professional regiment composed of lesser chieftains, these riders are not selected through connections, but rather by merit.

ids: Has unlocked unit trigger: Type Esho Cavalry
names: Has unlocked unit trigger: Type Esho Cavalry

units.name: Florentine Citizen Militia
units.desc: The shifting landscape of diplomacy and war in the Italian region dictates that we should not entrust our defense and sovereignty to paid condottieri. Instead, we should erect an able body of Florentine Citizen Militia, quick to mobilize and lacking no qualities when compared to any other troops, to defend our domain from prospecting conquerors.
units.whoText: Culture: Tuscan

units.name: Naft Throwers
units.desc: Using the secret of the Greek fire, these Naft Throwers throw incendiary grenades at the enemy, using that element in order to not only burn their opponents, but to sow confusion and panic in their ranks. They mainly serve to scare the enemy rather than kill.

ids: Has unlocked unit trigger: Type Naft Throwers
names: Has unlocked unit trigger: Type Naft Throwers

units.whoText: Has unlocked unit trigger: Type Naft Throwers

units.name: Andalusi Arquebusiers
units.desc: The Andalusi Arquebusiers are firearm infantry trained by the Andalusi exiles who filled the Maghrebi cities after the fall of Granada, keeping the gunpowder craft of the Nasrid emirate's last decades. They fought as shock troops at the Battle of the Three Kings.
units.whoText: (culture group: Amazigh or culture group: Maghrebi or culture: Andalusi)

units.name: Algiers Ojaq Janissaries
units.desc: The Algiers Ojaq Janissaries are the musketeer ojaq of the Algerian Regency, an Ottoman-trained Janissary garrison founded after the Barbarossa brothers took Algiers and steadily reinforced with Anatolian recruits. They hold the Kasbah and the coastal forts and elect their own Aga, who shares power with the Dey.
units.whoText: Country: Algiers

units.name: Iron-Helmet Musketeers
units.desc: Skilled soldiers who wear iron helmets for protection and wield muskets as their primary firearms, these troops have come to dominate the battlefields. They serve as infantry troops in various armies across Africa, under the banner of some of the most powerful rulers. Loading their muskets with black powder and lead balls, aiming and firing at their enemies from a distance, their thunderous volleys have stopped many charges in their tracks, whilst their iron helmets provide vital head protection during battles and skirmishes. These musketeers play a crucial role in the evolution of warfare, introducing firearms as a significant force on the battlefield.

units.name: Hungarian Hussars
units.desc: Drawing inspiration from the storied legacy of King Matthias I Corvinus' cavalry, this idea introduces the 'Royal Hussar Regiments,' granting a formidable edge to Hungary's light cavalry forces. With their swift and fearless charges, these regiments are a symbol of Hungarian martial prowess, proving indispensable on the battlefields of Europe.

units.name: Swiss Guard
units.desc: The Swiss Guard is an armed force, formed by unmarried catholic Swiss men, whose mission is to ensure the security of the Pope. Originally hired as a permanent mercenary unit, they became part of the armies of the Holy Father.

units.name: Mauricians
units.desc: The Mauricians are a very mobile infantry unit that shots its volleys by lines of shooters, so that while a line recharges their arms, the next is firing at the enemy. This rotation gives them a tremendous power over their enemies.

units.name: Tercio
units.desc: The Tercio is an elite military unit inside the Spanish Armies, famed for its battlefield formations. Considered some of the finest warriors in Western Europe, the Tercios are one of the region's first modern professional armies.
units.whoText: Culture group: Iberian; Religion group: Christianity

units.name: Sowar Cavalry
units.desc: The Sowar Cavalry is the heavy cavalry of the Mughals. They are notorious for their enduring discipline and their terrifying shock charge which eliminates any semblance of hope for the enemy.
units.whoText: Current age = Reformation, Current age = Absolutism, Current age = Revolutions; Country: Mughal

units.name: Winged Hussars
units.desc: Dressed in characteristic wings and donning illustrious armor, these cavalrymen are a force to be reckoned with when it comes to their powerful charges, dealing immense damage and shattering the enemy's morale.

units.name: Red Cannon
units.desc: Developed by a conjunction of imperial gunsmiths and known also as Hóngyípào, this piece of artillery is the epitome of perfection of Asian craftsmanship upon European designs. Based loosely on the Culverin models employed in the West, these cannons have received further improvements, increasing their firepower and reducing their weight.

units.name: Banner Cavalry
units.desc: Born on the steppes and raised in the hardships between battle and iron, these riders are the bringers of doom for those who seek to oppose our rule. Their devastating charges and mastery of warfare makes them a formidable opponent.

units.name: Ḡilmān
units.desc: The Ḡilmān are an elite infantrymen corps which took on the usage of firearms instead of relying on traditional weapons. Made of slave soldiers, the Ḡilmān swear absolute loyalty towards the Shah before anyone else.

units.name: Saxon Defensioner
units.desc: The Defensioner are veteran troops from the rough lands on the Bohemian border. Tasked with securing the passes in the Ore Mountains, these units will serve us well in battles on rough terrain.

units.name: Hessian Jäger
units.desc: Elite light troops composed of expert hunters. Their knowledge of our own terrain will increase our ability to fight in dense forests, although their equipment is not suited for prolonged fighting.

units.name: Gebirgsschützen
units.desc: These mountain shooters are unmatched in traversing alpine terrain and besting our foes in the treacherous mountain passes. Their light equipment and loose organization makes them perfectly equipped for high-altitude combat.

units.name: Modernized Helepolis
units.desc: The Helepolis has served many Byzantine emperors in the past. With the introduction of gunpowder and the advent of new siege machines of warfare, the city-taker artillery has now embraced its new deadly form.

units.name: Sub-Saharan Musketeers
units.desc: The Sub-Saharan Musketeers are the black musketeers of the Saadian armies, men brought north across the desert as captives and put to the matchlock in the garrison towns of Merrakš and Fas. The sultans prize a musket line with no clan behind it and no stake in a succession quarrel.
units.whoText: Culture group: Amazigh, Maghrebi

units.name: Hakkapeliitta
units.desc: The Hakkapeliitta were the fearsome Finnish cavalry known for their gruesome effectiveness on the battlefield. The name Hakkapeliitta is a Finnish modification of the names that the soldiers of the Holy Roman Empire gave them, stemming from their battle cry 'Hakkaa päälle!', or 'Hack on them!'/'Cut them down!'. The Hakkapeliitta were feared for their sudden and savage attacks that shocked the enemy into submission.

units.name: Caroleans
units.desc: The Caroleans are the Swedish and Finnish infantry of the Swedish Empire. Recruited from the peasantry, the Caroleans go under strict training and are renowned for invoking fear in the hearts of their enemies.

units.name: Scottish Highlander
units.desc: The noble clans of the Highlands are an invaluable asset to our military. With their old formations adapted to the age of muskets, which became famous as the 'Highland Charge', these clansmen will charge at the enemy and deliver a devastating blow to the enemies' morale with their broadswords.
units.whoText: Culture: Highland, Norse-Gael

units.name: Late Paik
units.desc: Paiks are foot soldiers of India who are renowned for their offensive and defensive versatility and their skill in archery. As the weapons develop, so does their portfolio of skills. Thus, the bows of the early eras have been replaced by the modern musket, yet their versatility still prevails.

units.name: Late Winged Hussars
units.desc: Dressed in characteristic wings and donning illustrious armor, these cavalrymen are a force to be reckoned with when it comes to their powerful charges, dealing immense damage and shattering the enemy's morale.

units.name: Tofangchi
units.desc: The Tofangchi are the musketeers of the empire. Although firearms have been in use before already, their presence has been highly irregular as many of the Persian military prefer to use their traditional weapon of bow and arrow. The regiments of the Tofangchi aim to change this as they are trained in the usage of the modern weaponry.

units.name: Tupchi
units.desc: The Tupchi - artillery-men - are a specialized military unit that focuses on the usage of cannons and siege weapons. Similar to the Tofangchi, the Tupchi are an example of modern warfare exercised by the Persian Empire.

units.name: Black Guard
units.desc: The Black Guard is an elite corps of slave soldiers: enslaved men, haratin, and free Muslims raised from childhood to a strict religious creed and drilled in archery, horsemanship, and musketry. They form the backbone of our army.
units.whoText: Country: Morocco

units.name: Prussian Grenadiers
units.desc: The Prussian Grenadiers are elite troops of the Prussian Army. Their role as vanguards in sieges and assaults requires them to be fearless fighters, recruited from among the strongest men in our country.

units.name: Bavarian Jäger
units.desc: Regiments of seasoned hunters and foresters. These units will be unmatched in forested terrain, able to hinder and harass our enemies if they dare to enter our forests.

units.name: Hajduk
units.desc: The Hajduk are a light infantry unit common across the Balkans and surrounding areas. Operating as autonomous bands, these frontiersmen are often driven to the mountains by fiscal oppression, legal disputes, or a desire for military glory, specializing in the disruption of supply lines and the ambushing of tax convoys.

units.name: Redcoats
units.desc: Redcoats is the name given to the English Line and Column Infantry, after the adoption of red coats by soldiers fighting in Ireland, and their generalization in the New Model Army.

units.name: Experimental Riflemen
units.desc: Elite marksmen equipped with the long-range Baker Rifle and trained to screen the main force in small independent pickets, Experimental Riflemen represent a modern vision of infantry combat formations.

units.name: Caçadores
units.desc: Caçadores (hunters), the Portuguese version of the German Jägers or the French Chasseurs, are an elite light infantry unit whose mission is the defense of the Portuguese territory.
units.whoText: (country: Portugal or culture: Portuguese); Religion group: Christianity

units.name: Gurkha
units.desc: Gurkha are troops of Nepali origins (as their name are quite interchangeable) who are infamous for their unbreakable bravery and discipline in combat.

units.name: Jazāyerchi
units.desc: The Jazāyerchi are the elite musketeers of the empire. Equipped with heavy flintlock muskets with superior firepower and accuracy and exposed to constant drilling, the Jazāyerchi manage to overcome even the most one-sided odds in battle.

units.name: Grenzhussar
units.desc: Stationed in border garrisons, these regiments of hussars will be able to patrol and secure the far reaches of our country, while keeping the strain on our treasury light.

units.name: Pandur Infantry
units.desc: Recruited from our Carpathian and Balkan lands, these light troops are well equipped to guard the peace in our border regions. Their knowledge of their homeland will make them a formidable opponent for any invader.

units.name: Grenzer Infantry
units.desc: Recruited from our Carpathian and Balkan lands, these light troops are well equipped to guard the peace in our border regions. Their knowledge of their homeland will make them a formidable opponent for any invader.

units.name: Grenadiers
units.desc: Evolved from earlier units equipped with explosives, these Grenadiers serve as elite vanguards for our armies. While the grenades from which their name comes are no longer their sole focus, their superior training makes them excellent assault troops.

units.name: Early Conquistadors
units.desc: Under the 'capitulations of conquests', men of the lower nobility or otherwise low status embark to conquer foreign lands for their kings.

units.name: Conquistadors
units.desc: A more established version of the Conquistador with a better insight on what they can aspire to. These men full of ambition will make empires crumble.

units.name: Footmen
units.desc: The backbone of every army, footmen comprise the majority of our marching troops, eager to sustain a frontline and defend our home from prospecting invaders.
units.whoText: not government: Steppe Horde

units.name: Archers
units.desc: Archers support our footmen with ranged fire, allowing them to advance towards enemy lines when attacking and also helping them better protect their position when defending.
units.whoText: not government: Steppe Horde

units.name: Footmen Levy
units.desc: The backbone of every army, footmen comprise the majority of our marching troops, eager to sustain a frontline and defend our home from prospecting invaders.
units.whoText: not government: Steppe Horde

units.name: Horsemen
units.desc: Lightly-armored fighters mounted upon swift horses, bands of Horsemen have the mobility to harass, charge, and pursue.

units.name: Armored Horsemen
units.desc: Horsemen who are more heavily armored, usually with some form of mail or full plate, to charge headlong into enemy ranks.

units.name: Camp Followers
units.desc: A motley crew of merchants and families of the soldiery, Camp Followers provide informal services to warbands on the march.
units.whoText: not government: Steppe Horde

units.name: Men-at-Arms
units.desc: Armored footmen outfitted with a medley of hand-to-hand weapons, Men-at-Arms are heavy melee infantry who can break through enemy formations.

units.name: Crossbowmen
units.desc: Crossbowmen are a type of ranged fire unit that harness the increased firepower of crossbows, a much more powerful, albeit slow-reloading, projectile weapon.

units.name: Handgonners
units.desc: Handgonners wield a new type of gunpowder-filled weapon that fires deadly lead shells, wreaking havoc on enemy lines, though they need to be fully protected as their handgonnes are very slow to reload.

units.name: Men-at-Arms
units.desc: Men-at-Arms

units.name: Cavalrymen
units.desc: Cavalrymen are light cavalry, sometimes armed with ranged weapons, used to attack enemy lines, although they may sometimes be ready to charge into close combat.

units.name: Heavy Cavalrymen
units.desc: A heavier type of cavalry, fully armored and trained for shock charges, thanks to its heavy armor and armament, which should lead to the disruption of the enemy line.

units.name: Houfnice
units.desc: It is believed modern howitzers have their name from the Houfnice artillery developed by the Hussites in the 15th century. These short-barreled guns were mounted on wagons and used on the field of battle to fire balls and canisters in support of the infantry.

units.name: Peasant Levy
units.desc: A Peasant Levy is formed by commoners summoned for military service by their Lord. The men are meant to bring their own equipment to battle, so the quality of newly created units can vary greatly.

units.name: Supply Carts
units.desc: The Supply Carts are the lifeline of any army wanting to venture outside home territories. They provided food to the men and the animals, extending the distance the army could travel before stopping to forage what can be very hostile lands.

units.name: Early Arquebusiers
units.desc: The arquebus is the evolution of the handgonne, making it a more reliable type of gunpowder weapon as it is easier and faster to reload, making it ideal for deploying larger gunpowder fire units.

units.name: Halberdiers
units.desc: Halberdiers are units of soldiers that wield polearms, such as halberds, which are used for close combat, both offensively and defensively.

units.name: Light Lancers
units.desc: Light Lancers are a type of light cavalry more focused on shock combat, as they use a charging lance, also wearing some degree of armor. However, they base their success on the battlefield on maintaining a high degree of mobility.

units.name: Lancers
units.desc: Strong cavalry armed with a lance, these shock troops are meant to break through enemy lines and devastate our foes' forces.

units.name: Falconet
units.desc: The Falconet is a light cannon developed in the 15th century as an evolution of the similar falcon, being more mobile while firing smaller caliber shots.

units.name: Matchlock Levy
units.desc: The development of the matchlock arquebus makes it possible to arm large numbers of soldiers with gunpowder weapons on a scale that was not possible in the Middle Ages.

units.name: Supply Convoy
units.desc: The transition from feudal levies to standing armies in the Discovery is allowing longer campaigns, creating the need to supply those soldiers for longer periods. That comes from the more organized Supply Convoy.

units.name: Arquebusiers
units.desc: A pike-and-shot formation consisting of a core of troops armed with firearms and protected by a phalanx of armored pikemen, the Arquebusiers are a formidable unit that cannot be easily countered.

units.name: Pikemen
units.desc: Pikemen are footmen armed with pikes, allowing them to form dense formations that easily confront enemy cavalry charges, thus negating the power of cavalry on the battlefield.

units.name: Pistoleers
units.desc: Pistoleers are light cavalrymen armed with pistols, a type of gunpowder weapon that is easier to carry and handle on horseback, but can also be used as a melee weapon, thanks to its heavy, reinforced grip.

units.name: Heavy Lancers
units.desc: Heavy Lancers are the heaviest type of shock cavalry possible, and feature fully armored armor and the finest shock lances. Their charges are designed to completely disrupt the enemy formation, and they are also much more protected from enemy fire at range.

units.name: Chambered Cannon
units.desc: The 16th century did not only see improvements in artillery maneuverability but also in the attempts at standardizing the size and weight of artillery pieces.

units.name: Flintlock Levy
units.desc: The flintlock musket has replaced the matchlock arquebus as the primary infantry weapon, providing greater and more accurate firepower while being easier to use and maintain.

units.name: Baggage Train
units.desc: The generalization of standing armies in the Reformation is further developing the supply needs of their soldiers, the use of a Baggage Train that follows the advance of the armies becoming commonplace.

units.name: Hunters
units.desc: Hunters are light infantry designed to attack enemy formations from long range as they approach, attempting to disorganize them and make their own firepower much less effective.

units.name: Musketeers
units.desc: The musketeers are the elite fighting force of the royal household. Being a musketeer is a position of great prestige and only nobles with years of military service are allowed to join the company's ranks.

units.name: Hussars
units.desc: The hussars were originally light cavalry troops originating in Central Europe that were used for scouting, but with the decline of the old feudal army they were switched over to professional regiments.

units.name: Gallop Cavalry
units.desc: Gallop Cavalry is a shock unit that charges the enemy with long cavalry sabers, protected with a certain degree of armor, which is a good balance between mobility and forcefulness.

units.name: Royal Mortar
units.desc: From the second half of the 17th century the use of artillery on the battlefield became more widespread. The troops were now able to move their field guns with much more ease and speed.

units.name: Militiamen
units.desc: The generalization of muskets as the main firearms during the 17th century allows local Militiamen units to be deployed as reserve and support units for the main armies on the battlefield.

units.name: Wagon Train
units.desc: The growth in the size of armies during the Absolutism is making their logistics increasingly complex, making each army dependent on its own Wagon Train to maintain its combat performance in the field.

units.name: Sharpshooters
units.desc: Sharpshooters are a type of light infantry unit made up of the best marksmen, who use rifles with a longer range, making them better at skirmishing and disrupting enemy formations while maneuvering.

units.name: Fusiliers
units.desc: Fusiliers are the backbone of our armies, armed with a modern ranged rifle and a bayonet that can be attached to it and enables the possibility of massed charges into enemy ranks.

units.name: Light Dragoons
units.desc: Light Dragoons are a type of light cavalry that can move, dismount, and shoot at the enemy with the rifles they carry, but are also armed with cavalry sabers, which allow them to charge the enemy if the opportunity arises.

units.name: Cuirassiers
units.desc: Keeping up with the changing times, Cuirassiers are heavy cavalry that have discarded lances in favor of pistols and sabers as their primary weapon.

units.name: Flying Battery
units.desc: Artillery is devastating on the battlefield, but completely useless if the enemy does not enter its firing range. A Flying Battery has the capability of relocating itself to where it is most needed and quickly redeploy before any enemy's retaliation.

units.name: Conscripts
units.desc: Reluctant soldiers obligated to fight, massed Conscripts can overwhelm a trained army through numbers alone.

units.name: Logistics Corps
units.desc: A strict operation consisting of supply trains and an efficient bureaucracy, Logistics Corps represent the pinnacle of military organization during the Revolutions to support vast armies.

units.desc: Lightly-armored riders mounted on swift camels, Camelry excel in the arid wastes of the desert, harassing enemies and exploiting their superior mobility on open terrain.

units.name: Granadan Jinetes
units.desc: Born of the Andalusi frontier wars, the jinetes ride light, unarmored horses and fight with javelins, short swords, and the heart-shaped leather adarga. Their hit-and-run skirmishes, drawn from Berber tactics carried across the Strait, dictate the pace of warfare on the Iberian peninsula, and neighboring realms swiftly imitate them in turn.

units.name: Tornadizos
units.desc: Drawn out of the Christian kingdoms into Nasrid pay, these men keep their own faith and their own priests while they serve us — the frontier calls them tornadizos regardless, a word it throws at anyone who changes sides in either direction. They bring lance-and-plate technique into our armies, and their armored charge mirrors the gendarmes of Castile and Aragon, yet they ride beside the Granadan Jinetes under the green banners of our emirate. Recruitment is slow, for such men are few, and each one trained in the Christian art of war makes our cavalry an enemy unlike any other Andalusi force the frontier has seen.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; (country: Granada or culture: Andalusi); Region: Iberia

units.name: Ṯaḡrī
units.desc: Drawn from the marcher villages of the ṯuḡūr, the ṯaḡrī fight as foot spearmen who know every pass and watercourse of the Andalusi frontier. They train cheaply on village rations, march for weeks on what a Castilian column eats in days, and answer the call at the first beacon. Their weapons are plain and their pay is meager, yet no force in Iberia matches their endurance along the mountain marches.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; Country: Granada; Region: Iberia

units.name: Sometent
units.desc: The Sometent are the levied urban and rural militias of the Catalan lands — the sometent called out by bell and horn whenever the frontier is threatened. Armed with spear and shield, they are not professional soldiers but defenders of hearth and village, and their stubborn resilience in the face of raid and incursion makes them harder to break than their numbers would suggest.
units.whoText: (dlc: Across The Pillars and culture: Catalan)

units.name: Milicia Concejil
units.desc: The Milicia Concejil are the town levies of the Castilian and Leonese municipalities — the concejos of the Meseta obligated by royal charter to furnish men for local defense and frontier service. Drawn from the burghers and tradesmen of the walled towns, they are a cheap and accessible force whose greatest strength is their familiarity with the terrain they are sworn to protect.
units.whoText: (Has estate privilege = Caballeros Villanos and not reform: Santa Hermandad and dlc: Across The Pillars and culture: Castilian, Asturleonese)

units.name: Caballería de Cuantía
units.desc: The Caballería de Cuantía are the property-qualified horsemen of Castile — men of sufficient wealth to maintain horse and arms, but below the rank of the high nobility. Riding in the light jinete style, these mid-rank cavalrymen fill the space between the great lords' retinues and the foot levies of the towns, providing the Castilian crown with a broad base of mounted manpower in exchange for exemption from the common tribute — a narrower privilege than an hidalgo's, but privilege enough to keep a horse.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; Country: Castile, Spain; Has estate privilege = Regimiento; Region: Iberia

units.name: Mutaṭawwi'a
units.desc: The mutaṭawwi'a are the volunteers of the Granadan frontier — devout men who ride the raiding season for the promise of paradise and a share of the plunder rather than for a wage, many of them gathered around some local morabito whose reputation for holiness draws them in. Light and fast, they strike at the Christian marches with javelin and sword before melting back into the sierra. They are not the sultan's salaried frontier horsemen and do not pretend to be: what they bring is numbers and fervor, and they disperse when the season ends.

units.name: Mesnaderos
units.desc: The Mesnaderos are the royal retinue cavalry of the Pyrenean crowns — the armored household knights who ride at the direct service of the king of Navarre or Aragon. Organized under the ancient obligation of the mesnada, these warriors are bound by personal loyalty and contract to their sovereign, forming a reliable core of experienced heavy cavalry that can be dispatched where the feudal levy would be too slow or unreliable.

units.name: Granadan Crossbowmen
units.desc: The Granadan Crossbowmen carry a weapon Granada borrowed rather than inherited: Ibn Huḏayl, writing for Muḥammad V himself, calls it the qaḍīb afranjī — the Frankish bow. We took it up from the frontier we fight on, and our workshops now turn out its nuts and tillers to a standard pattern in quantity. Deployed before the main line, a crossbowman needs a season's training where a bowman needs a lifetime, and his bolt punches through armor that would stop an arrow.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; (country: Granada or culture: Andalusi); Culture: Andalusi

units.name: Mulaṯṯamūn Spearmen
units.desc: The Mulaṯṯamūn Spearmen are the Ṣanhāja warriors of the western Sahara, named for the liṯām they never set aside — the Lamtūna clansmen whose ranked spear formations carried the strict Mālikī reform doctrine of Ibn Yāsīn, and afterwards the arms of Yūsuf ibn Tāšfīn, from the Saharan erg to the Ebro valley. Their front rank sets the long pike and the ranks behind loose the javelin, every man of them behind an oryx-hide lamt shield, veiled so that only the sockets of the eyes are seen. Their high morale derives from a religious commitment that no purely secular military tradition can match. The empire those spearmen built is long fallen, but the Maghreb has never forgotten how they fought, and our Ṣanhāja polity fields their heavy-foot corps still.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; Culture group: Amazigh, Maghrebi; Culture: Sanhaja

units.name: Ahl Tīnmal Spearmen
units.desc: The Ahl Tīnmal Spearmen are the Atlas-mountain spearmen of Tīnmal: Ibn Tūmart's refuge in the High Atlas, and the shrine his movement tended at his tomb until the Marinids razed it. They were drawn first from the Harga, his own people, and afterwards from the wider Masmuda confederations. They carry the heavy spear and round shield and fight in close order. What their movement overthrew was not a lesser sort of soldier but a state: by the 1120s the Almoravid administration was issuing contradictory orders, and its armies were largely no longer composed of Almoravids at all. This is the corps the caliphate was built upon, and our Masmuda state raises it still, charged with the institutional pride of an empire that once unified the entire western Muslim world.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; Culture group: Amazigh, Maghrebi; Culture: Masmuda

units.name: Tuareg Camelry
units.desc: The Tuareg Camelry are the mahrī riders of the deep Sahara — men the Arabic geographers count among the Ṣanhāja and know by their veils, mounted on racing dromedaries bred for speed across the great erg and hamada, carrying the long lance and the takouba for the close work after a camel charge has scattered a column. They raid the caravan roads and they also guard them, taking payment to escort and to guide, and taxing the traffic wherever they hold the wells. Three days of march where horse cavalry must halt for water makes them masters of corridors no settled army can police. This camelry tradition gives our confederations a raiding and long-range patrol arm that no rival within a thousand leagues of the desert can match.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; Culture group: Amazigh, Maghrebi; Culture: Tuareg; (dlc: Across The Pillars and culture: Tuareg, Eastern Amazigh)

units.name: Zenata Cavalry
units.desc: The Zenata Cavalry are light horsemen of the Zenata Berber confederations — the Banū Marīn, Banū 'Abd al-Wād, and Maghrāwa — whose pastoral upbringing makes them masters of swift desert and steppe warfare. Each warrior brings his own mount, his own kit, and his own retinue of kinsmen, requiring no royal armory or extended training to field. This pool of tribal light cavalry gives every Maghrebi sultan a fast-moving striking arm that the heavier Christian and eastern-Muslim cavalry cannot easily catch in open country.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; Culture group: Amazigh, Maghrebi; Culture: Zenati; (dlc: Across The Pillars and culture: Zenati)

units.name: Ṣanhāja Camel Cavalry
units.desc: The Ṣanhāja Camel Cavalry are the camel and light-horse riders of the Saharan Ṣanhāja — the Lamtūna and the Masūfa, veiled men whose fathers built an empire reaching from the Senegal to the Ebro. That day is past. The century turns against them, and the dynasties rising now are Zanata and Masmuda. What has not changed is the desert, which they still cross as no one else can: their camels carry them over distances no horse cavalry can attempt, and their light-spear charge is a Maghrebi answer to the heavy lance of the Iberian and Sahelian powers. This Ṣanhāja desert-cavalry tradition gives our armies an unmatched logistical and maneuver reach across the southern frontier.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; Culture group: Amazigh, Maghrebi; Culture: Sanhaja; (dlc: Across The Pillars and culture: Sanhaja)

units.name: Masmuda Atlas Infantry
units.desc: The Masmuda Atlas Infantry are the heavy spearmen of the Masmuda Berber confederations of the Atlas mountains — farmers of the high valleys who muster for a season and return to their terraces, as they did long before the Almohad caliphate and long after it fell. Their forebears marched in the armies that swept the Maghreb and the Iberian peninsula in the twelfth century, and they carry that memory in the close formations the mountains taught them, suited to broken ground and to receiving heavy Christian cavalry. This Masmuda tradition gives every Maghrebi state a heavy infantry corps that no purely cavalry rival can easily break in close-quarter combat.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; Culture group: Amazigh, Maghrebi; Culture: Masmuda; (dlc: Across The Pillars and culture: Masmuda)

units.name: Kabyle Skirmishers
units.desc: The Kabyle Skirmishers are the highland fighters of the Djurdjura and the Babor east of Algiers — the Zwāwa of the Arabic geographers, counted subjects of the Hafsid sultan at Béjaïa and paying him nothing. Their kinsmen have made empires before now: the Kutāma of the eastern hills were the army that carried the Fatimids into Ifrīqiya, and Ṣanhāja of the same stock founded the Zirid and Hammadid dynasties after them. They harass a marching column with thrown spears and are gone into ground no formation can follow. This mountain-warfare tradition gives the Maghrebi armies a flanking arm for the hilly, wooded country where pitched-battle infantry cannot maneuver.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; Culture group: Amazigh, Maghrebi; Culture: Kabyle; (dlc: Across The Pillars and culture: Kabyle)

units.name: Hilālī Bedouin Cavalry
units.desc: The Hilālī Bedouin Cavalry are the Arab-tribal light horsemen of the Banū Hilāl and Banū Sulaym — pastoralists who came west out of Upper Egypt across generations rather than in one wave, and whose slow settlement of the steppe has remade its speech and its rural order for good. By our own day the Riyāḥ and the Dawāwida make kings and unmake them, and the sultans between Tunis and Tlemcen court them with marriages, with tax-farms, and with grants of land and revenue to their chiefs. They ride to us under their own captains and on their own mounts, and they will not be told where to camp. This Arab-Bedouin tradition gives our armies a striking arm whose mobility and tribal numbers complement the Berber confederations without competing for the same kinship-recruitment pool.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; Culture group: Amazigh, Maghrebi; Culture: Tunisian, Algerian, Eastern Amazigh; (dlc: Across The Pillars and culture: Tunisian, Algerian, Eastern Amazigh)

units.name: Late Granadan Jinetes
units.desc: Centuries of Granadan Jinetes refinement now yield a more disciplined, better-equipped horseman. Mail shirts and longer lances complement the traditional javelin, yet the core doctrine of speed, harassment, and feigned retreat remains the trademark of the Granadan light horse.

units.name: Late Tornadizos
units.desc: Generations of Tornadizos settlement have built a standing class of armored cavalry whose training and equipment now match the best Christian knights of Iberia. Their lances are longer, their plate heavier, and their numbers no longer depend on the frontier's whim. The Andalusi heavy horse has come of age, fielded under our own banners against the kingdoms whose technique once defined them.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; (country: Granada or culture: Andalusi); Region: Iberia

units.name: Late Ṯaḡrī
units.desc: Generations of Ṯaḡrī service have settled the corps into a hereditary class of frontier wardens. The march is in their bones, the passes mapped in their grandfathers' songs, the drill inherited from their fathers' company. They still draw a peasant's wage and a peasant's bread, yet a column of them can hold the sierra through a full season of campaign while a knightly retinue would starve in a fortnight.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; Country: Granada; Region: Iberia

units.name: Alabarderos
units.desc: The Alabarderos are the halberd-bearing guard of the royal person — a single company of a few score men, raised to stand at the door of the chamber rather than in the line of battle. Their polearms guard the monarch as much as they grace the court, and a king who finds himself relying on them in the field has already lost the field.

units.name: Milicia Irmandinha
units.desc: The Milicia Irmandinha are the militia forces raised by the Galician brotherhoods — the Irmandades of the mid-fifteenth century that united the towns of Galicia against the tyranny of the great noble houses. Lightly armed but fiercely motivated, these citizen soldiers reflect the communal solidarity of the Galician urban guilds and small landholders who chose collective action over submission to the señorial yoke.

units.name: Hermandad Infantry
units.desc: The Hermandad Infantry are the organized militia companies of the Santa Hermandad — the Holy Brotherhood established to provide Castile with a standing internal force capable of maintaining order across the vast meseta. Unlike the old feudal levies, these men are raised and paid by the towns but answer to royal magistrates rather than to local lords, and their discipline makes them a far more reliable instrument of the new centralized state than any baronial host.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; Reform: Santa Hermandad; (dlc: Across The Pillars and reform: Santa Hermandad and culture: Castilian, Asturleonese)

units.name: Coronelías
units.desc: The Coronelías are the infantry Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba shaped in the Italian wars: several companies held together as one body under a colonel where a captain had commanded before, with pike, sword and arquebus each given their own place in the line rather than thrown in together. The tercio is not yet named; that waits on an ordinance out of Genoa. But this is the formation it will be named for, and the men who learn their trade here are the ones who will fill it.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; (country: Castile or (country: Spain and culture: Castilian))

units.name: Aṣ-Ṣaqāliba al-Mutaqaddimūn
units.desc: We raise the first generation of the revived corps, the mutaqaddimūn who came before. We name them the aṣ-Ṣaqāliba al-Judud, the New Ṣaqāliba, to set them apart from the al-Qudamā' of Cordoba's lost golden age. Bound to the dār and to the household, they owe nothing to the frontier clans or the old Arab families.

units.name: Guardias de Ornato
units.desc: The Guardias de Ornato are the ceremonial halberdier guard of the Castilian court, richly attired successors of the Alabarderos who escort the sovereign with lance and halberd.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; (country: Castile or (country: Spain and culture: Castilian))

units.name: Miquelets
units.desc: The Miquelets are the irregular light infantry of the Catalan mountains — bands of tough highland fighters who have served Catalan lords and Castilian kings alike in the passes of the Pyrenees and the ravines of the eastern coast. Moving faster than regular troops and vanishing before pursuit can be organized, these guerrilla soldiers excel in the ambush and the raid, turning the rugged terrain of their homeland into their greatest weapon.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; (country: Catalonia or (country: Spain and culture: Aragonese, Catalan)); Reformation or later; Culture: Catalan

units.name: Infantería de Marina
units.desc: The Infantería de Marina are the marines of the Castilian navy — the soldiers who ride aboard our warships to storm enemy decks, hold coastal positions, and spearhead amphibious landings. Organized as standing companies in the grand tradition of the tercio, these fighting sailors are equally at home on the crowded gangway of a galley and in the breach of a coastal fortress, making them the sharp edge of our overseas power projection.
units.whoText: DLC: Across The Pillars; (country: Castile or (country: Spain and culture: Castilian)); Has ports

units.name: Aṣ-Ṣaqāliba al-Muta'aḵḵirūn
units.desc: A reforming hand reorganizes the corps for its second age. Drill is standardized, the musket replaces older arms, and the rolls of the dār swell beyond anything the Aṣ-Ṣaqāliba al-Mutaqaddimūn knew. The later Ṣaqāliba, the muta'aḵḵirūn, become a permanent pillar of the host rather than a revival still proving itself.

units.name: Guich Cavalry
units.desc: The Guich Cavalry are the standing cavalry of the Moroccan Maḵzan — jīš tribesmen, of usually Arab origin, settled on arḍ al-jayš and holding their plots free of tax for as long as they ride. They are soldier-cultivators and not nobles, with no lineage of their own to fall back on, and that is precisely why the sultan trusts them: a corps whose standing depends entirely upon the crown. Mounted and paid in land, they carry the sultan's writ into country where a tax collector alone would not be heeded, and they cost the treasury less than any force that must be paid in coin.

units.name: An-Niẓām al-Jadīd
units.desc: A sweeping reorganization remakes the corps into a niẓām jadīd, a New Order in the manner of the great gunpowder armies of the age. Uniform companies, magazine drills, and a chain of slave-officers risen from the ranks give the household a modern infantry who answer to the throne and no one else. Their very name proclaims the break with all that came before.
